reason: The text explicitly establishes and encourages strict hierarchical structures. God appoints Moses and Aaron as leaders with authority over the Israelites. Most significantly, in Exodus 18, Jethro advises Moses to establish a hierarchical system of judges organized in tiers: 'captains of thousands, captains of hundreds, captains of fifties, and captains of tens' (שָׂרֵי אֲלָפִים, שָׂרֵי מֵאוֹת, שָׂרֵי חֲמִשִּׁים, שָׂרֵי עֲשָׂרוֹת). Moses explicitly implements this hierarchical structure, selecting qualified men for leadership positions. The text demonstrates that hierarchy is not only important but actively mandated for proper governance and order.
